notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so the opus tier is "unavailable" in per_rule. Runs were made at 58f6318 with the uncommitted rule changes (skill_hash 9faec678...).

Naming changed since 93873be and is graded against the current text. The fetch sentence now decides with "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ## Naming). The generic-name sentence now decides with "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name." (same list), so data bound from the "data" key no longer counts. The previous sweep counted it in every run that used it.

Naming, violating runs out of four per sentence: fetch_* returning {:error, reason}: 1 of 4 (haiku-2: fetch_string/2, fetch_integer/2, fetch_map/2). Generic name: 1 of 4 (haiku-1: required_string/2, required_integer/2, required_map/2 take the whole payload in a parameter named data). Under the 93873be text all four runs would have been violated, because each binds data from the "data" key.

The `with` rule changed since 93873be and is graded against the current text. The one-step sentence now decides with "With one step there is nothing to chain, and a `with` makes the reader look for the other steps. Use `case`, which shows both outcomes in one place" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ### Chain fallible steps with `with`). The 93873be text already ended its first paragraph with "Use `case` when there is only one step."; the change adds the reason and an example. The else sentence is unchanged.

`with`, violating runs out of four per sentence: one-step with: 2 of 4 (haiku-1 line 107, haiku-2 line 105, both a one-step with inside a per-type clause). Large else block: 0 of 4 (no run wrote an else).

Borderline calls under the new Naming text: sonnet-2 line 110 rebinds data to the parsed struct it stores in Event's data field, counted as carrying the payload's key name. haiku-2's body (line 92) is not counted, as the previous sweep did not count base or envelope. haiku-1's data parameter is counted because it receives the payload at lines 83, 98, 99 and 101, not only the "data" value.

Unchanged rules follow the previous sweep's standard: a bare _ -> in a key-lookup case is a match-every-shape violation (as baseline-sonnet-2) while %{} -> is clean; Map.get on required keys counts under the required-keys rule, not the struct rule (as baseline-opus-1); a parse_data/2 catch-all that routes every other type to payments is a violation (as skill-sonnet-2).

Verified in the scratch folder: all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with --warnings-as-errors; doctests pass (haiku-1 1, haiku-2 1, sonnet-1 3, sonnet-2 3); a probe of 12 payloads confirmed the missing and invalid results quoted above. Transcripts show each run reading only SKILL.md.
